meta.title: DWP Midterm — 60 Unique Questions
meta.description: Comprehensive midterm practice set covering Fetch API, REST, Node.js, browser architecture, and async JavaScript.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture's completed fetch example, which JavaScript expression creates a new image element equivalent to `document.createElement('img')`?

options.label: A
options.text: `document.newImage()`

options.label: B
options.text: `image.create()`

options.label: C
options.text: `new Img()`

options.label: D
options.text: `new Image()`

questions.explanationMd: `new Image()` creates an HTML image element, similar to creating an `` element with `document.createElement('img')`.

questions.questionMd: Which command is used to serve local files over HTTP so that `fetch()` can access them during development?

options.label: A
options.text: `python3 -m http.server`

options.label: B
options.text: `python3 -m fetch-server`

options.label: C
options.text: `npm start http`

options.label: D
options.text: `node server.js`

questions.explanationMd: `python3 -m http.server` starts a simple local HTTP server, avoiding browser restrictions that can occur with `file://` URLs.

questions.questionMd: Which HTTP method does a browser send automatically whenever you navigate to a URL in the address bar?

options.label: A
options.text: DELETE

options.label: B
options.text: PUT

options.label: C
options.text: POST

options.label: D
options.text: GET

questions.explanationMd: Normal browser navigation sends an HTTP `GET` request to retrieve the resource at the entered URL.

questions.questionMd: What is the key difference between calling `response.text()` and `response.json()` inside a `fetch()` response handler?

options.label: A
options.text: `response.text()` returns a Promise while `response.json()` returns a value directly

options.label: B
options.text: `response.json()` automatically parses the response string into a JavaScript object

options.label: C
options.text: `response.text()` is faster because it skips validation

options.label: D
options.text: `response.json()` only works with REST APIs, not local files

questions.explanationMd: Both methods are asynchronous, but `response.json()` parses the body as JSON and resolves to the resulting JavaScript value.

questions.questionMd: How does the lecture describe XMLHttpRequest (XHR) compared to the Fetch API?

options.label: A
options.text: Simpler but less flexible

options.label: B
options.text: Clunky and harder to use

options.label: C
options.text: More secure and widely supported

options.label: D
options.text: Faster and more reliable

questions.explanationMd: XHR is the older request API and is usually considered more verbose and harder to use than the Promise-based Fetch API.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following is listed in the lecture as one of the HTTP methods used in RESTful API requests?

options.label: A
options.text: DELETE

options.label: B
options.text: QUERY

options.label: C
options.text: FETCH

options.label: D
options.text: STREAM

questions.explanationMd: RESTful APIs commonly use HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what is the problem with using ordinary inner functions (closures) as callbacks in `fetch().then()` chains inside a class method?

options.label: A
options.text: Closures capture the value of `this` at the time the outer function is defined rather than at the time it is called, leading to a stale reference in long-lived operations

options.label: B
options.text: Closures defined inside a method are garbage-collected before the `fetch()` promise resolves, causing a null reference error when the callback eventually fires

options.label: C
options.text: Each function has its own `this` value, so closures do not automatically inherit the `this` binding of their enclosing class method

options.label: D
options.text: The `fetch()` API enforces strict mode internally, which prevents closures from accessing any variable declared in the outer function scope with the `var` keyword

questions.explanationMd: Ordinary functions have their own `this`, so callbacks passed to `.then()` may not keep the class instance as `this` unless they are bound or arrow functions are used.

questions.questionMd: Which combination of components makes up the Chrome browser's architecture as described in the lecture?

options.label: A
options.text: The SpiderMonkey interpreter, the CSS rendering pipeline, and the WebAssembly execution environment for compiled code modules

options.label: B
options.text: The TCP socket library, the DNS resolver module, and the ExpressJS routing engine embedded into the browser at compile time

options.label: C
options.text: The V8 JavaScript engine (with parser, execution engine, and garbage collector), the JavaScript runtime, and the DOM API implementation

options.label: D
options.text: The npm package manager, the NodeJS API implementation, and a built-in HTTP server for serving static web assets locally

questions.explanationMd: Chrome uses V8 to execute JavaScript, plus browser-provided runtime features and DOM APIs for interacting with web pages.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture's definition, what is a “gotcha” in programming?

options.label: A
options.text: A valid construct that works as documented but is counter-intuitive and almost invites mistakes because it is easy to invoke and unexpected in its outcome

options.label: B
options.text: A deprecated API function that still exists in the language specification for backward compatibility but produces incorrect results when called in strict mode environments

options.label: C
options.text: A deliberate bug intentionally left in a codebase by a developer to test whether automated testing pipelines are comprehensive enough to catch subtle logic errors

options.label: D
options.text: A security vulnerability in a programming language runtime that attackers can exploit to execute arbitrary code by supplying malformed input to a parsing function

questions.explanationMd: A gotcha is behavior that is technically valid but surprising enough that developers commonly make mistakes with it.

questions.questionMd: Which built-in JavaScript array method is used in the lecture to reorder album objects by year?

options.label: A
options.text: `.reduce()`

options.label: B
options.text: `.filter()`

options.label: C
options.text: `.sort()`

questions.explanationMd: The `.sort()` method reorders array elements, typically using a comparator function for custom ordering.

questions.questionMd: What does CORS stand for?

options.label: A
options.text: Client-Only Resource Serialization, a browser policy that restricts JavaScript from reading binary resources loaded from external CDN servers

options.label: B
options.text: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing

options.label: C
options.text: Controlled Object Request Standard, an HTTP extension that governs how request headers are validated before the server processes the payload

options.label: D
options.text: Cross-Origin Response Security, an encryption layer added to HTTP responses that prevents man-in-the-middle interception of API data in transit

questions.explanationMd: CORS stands for Cross-Origin Resource Sharing, a browser security mechanism for controlled cross-origin requests.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following best describes a RESTful API?

options.label: A
options.text: A protocol for rendering HTML pages dynamically using query strings

options.label: B
options.text: An interface that exclusively uses the POST method to exchange data

options.label: C
options.text: An API that only works with browser-side JavaScript and cannot be accessed from a server

options.label: D
options.text: A URL-based API that uses HTTP methods and sends requests to a base endpoint

questions.explanationMd: RESTful APIs expose resources through URLs and use HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, what does TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) define?

options.label: A
options.text: The mapping between domain names and IP addresses maintained by distributed name servers across the internet

options.label: B
options.text: The structure and syntax of HTTP request and response messages exchanged between a browser and a web server

options.label: C
options.text: The data format used for sending information over the network wire, and it can be used for HTTP, FTP, and other protocols

options.label: D
options.text: The encryption standard applied to HTTPS traffic to protect data transmitted between clients and servers

questions.explanationMd: In the lecture framing, TCP is the lower-level transport protocol used underneath application protocols such as HTTP and FTP.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture summary, after the server software receives an HTTP request, what is the correct sequence of actions it takes?

options.label: A
options.text: The server software parses the message, creates an HTTP response, and then the server OS sends that response to the client over TCP

options.label: B
options.text: The server software binds to a new port, sends an HTTP GET request back to the client to confirm receipt, then closes the connection

options.label: C
options.text: The server software immediately sends an empty 200 OK response and then asynchronously processes the request body in the background

options.label: D
options.text: The server software forwards the raw TCP packet to the DNS server, which translates it and routes the reply back to the client browser

questions.explanationMd: A server program reads and parses the incoming request, prepares an HTTP response, and the operating system handles sending it over TCP.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following best describes a JavaScript Promise?

options.label: A
options.text: A synchronous function that immediately returns a value

options.label: B
options.text: A built-in timer that delays code execution by a specified amount

options.label: C
options.text: An object that handles asynchronous operations

options.label: D
options.text: A special array type used to store multiple fetch results

questions.explanationMd: A Promise represents the eventual result of an asynchronous operation, either fulfilled or rejected.

questions.questionMd: What does `JSON.parse()` accept as its argument?

options.label: A

options.label: C

questions.questionMd: What is the key difference between the DOM API used in Chrome and the NodeJS API?

options.label: A
options.text: The DOM API handles TCP socket connections and port binding, while the NodeJS API handles HTML parsing and CSS rendering

options.label: B
options.text: The DOM API uses the V8 engine for execution while the NodeJS API uses a different interpreter called SpiderMonkey for server tasks

options.label: C
options.text: The DOM API is written in JavaScript and runs only on Linux servers, while the NodeJS API is written in C++ and runs inside browsers

options.label: D
options.text: The DOM API provides JavaScript libraries to interact with a web page, while the NodeJS API provides libraries useful for creating server programs

questions.explanationMd: The DOM API is browser-oriented for page interaction, while NodeJS provides APIs for server-side tasks such as files, networking, and HTTP servers.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following data types is natively preserved when a JavaScript object is serialized to JSON using `JSON.stringify()`?

options.label: A
options.text: Date objects

options.label: B
options.text: `undefined` values

options.label: C
options.text: Numbers

options.label: D
options.text: Functions

questions.explanationMd: JSON natively represents strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, objects, and null; functions and `undefined` are not preserved as normal values.

questions.questionMd: How does NodeJS handle the complexity of network sockets when building a web server?

options.label: A
options.text: NodeJS uses the V8 engine's built-in socket library to open encrypted connections on all available network ports

options.label: B
options.text: NodeJS abstracts socket management away so developers do not need to think about sockets directly

options.label: C
options.text: NodeJS requires developers to manually create and bind sockets before attaching any HTTP request listeners

options.label: D
options.text: NodeJS delegates all socket creation to the browser's DOM API, which then forwards messages to the server program

questions.explanationMd: NodeJS provides higher-level server APIs so developers can listen for requests without manually managing raw sockets in typical web-server code.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, can NodeJS be used for purposes other than building web servers?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, NodeJS can be used to write general-purpose JavaScript scripts that are completely unrelated to web servers

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, but only if the scripts use the DOM API, because NodeJS was designed as a bridge between browser JavaScript and server JavaScript

options.label: C
options.text: No, NodeJS requires an active internet connection at all times and cannot run JavaScript files that make no network requests

options.label: D
options.text: No, NodeJS is exclusively designed for server-side HTTP handling and cannot execute scripts that do not involve network connections

questions.explanationMd: NodeJS is a JavaScript runtime that can run many kinds of scripts, not only web servers.

questions.questionMd: When handling a form's `submit` event in JavaScript, what must you call to prevent the page from refreshing?

options.label: D

questions.explanationMd: Calling `event.preventDefault()` stops the browser's default form submission behavior, which normally reloads or navigates the page.

questions.questionMd: Which of the following best describes the “fulfilled” state of a Promise?

options.label: D
options.text: The Promise is waiting for a `.then()` handler to be attached

questions.explanationMd: A fulfilled Promise is one whose asynchronous operation completed successfully and produced a value.

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture, why can multiple images load in parallel even though JavaScript is single-threaded?

options.label: A
options.text: JavaScript uses Web Workers internally for all image element operations, with each Image object spawning its own dedicated worker thread to manage the download lifecycle

options.label: B
options.text: The browser batches all image requests into a single multiplexed HTTP/2 stream that the JavaScript engine processes sequentially but displays simultaneously after all bytes arrive

options.label: C
options.text: Image loading is handled entirely by the operating system's DNS resolver and network stack, which feeds completed image buffers directly into the browser's graphics memory

options.label: D
options.text: The browser itself is multi-threaded and multi-process, so network requests and image decoding happen in browser threads outside the JavaScript runtime

questions.explanationMd: JavaScript execution may be single-threaded, but browsers use separate internal threads and processes for networking, decoding, and rendering work.

questions.questionMd: According to the well-known ports listed in the lecture, which port number is used by the Secure Shell (SSH) protocol?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Port 22, which is the standard port assigned to the Secure Shell protocol for encrypted remote access

options.label: C
options.text: Port 21, which is the port number assigned to the File Transfer Protocol for uploading and downloading files remotely

options.label: D
options.text: Port 443, which is the port number reserved for HTTPS and is sometimes mistaken for the SSH port by new developers

questions.explanationMd: SSH uses TCP port 22 by default for encrypted remote shell access.

questions.questionMd: What is “binding” in the context of running a server process?

options.label: A
options.text: Compiling JavaScript source code into native machine code before the NodeJS runtime begins accepting HTTP requests

options.label: B
options.text: Establishing a persistent TCP connection between two servers so they can exchange data without repeating the handshake

options.label: C
options.text: Encrypting the server's IP address so that DNS queries return a hashed value instead of the actual numerical address

options.label: D
options.text: Telling the operating system which port number to associate with the server process so it can receive incoming messages

questions.explanationMd: Binding associates a running server process with a port, so the operating system can deliver incoming network traffic on that port to the process.

questions.questionMd: Why does using `require('express')` in a NodeJS file fail if Express has not been installed first?

options.label: D
options.text: Because Express requires a valid HTTPS certificate to be present in the project directory before the module can be loaded

questions.explanationMd: Express is a third-party package, so it must be installed with npm before NodeJS can load it using `require('express')`.

questions.questionMd: What happens when you call `console.log('nodejs')` inside the NodeJS runtime?

options.label: D

questions.questionMd: According to the lecture summary, what is the correct sequence of steps that occurs when you navigate to a URL in your browser?

options.label: A
options.text: The browser binds to a local port, then calls `http.createServer()` to intercept the server's response before rendering it

options.label: B
options.text: The browser creates an HTTP GET request, then the operating system sends that request to the server over TCP

options.label: C
options.text: The operating system sends a DNS query, then the browser directly opens a socket to the resolved IP address and fetches the page

options.label: D
options.text: The browser parses the HTML response first, then sends an HTTP GET request to download any external CSS and JavaScript files

questions.explanationMd: At a high level, browser navigation creates an HTTP GET request and the operating system/network stack sends it to the remote server over TCP.

questions.questionMd: In the lecture's chained fetch example, what is the correct order of asynchronous operations?

options.label: A
options.text: `fetch` and `response.text()` run simultaneously before any handlers fire

options.label: B
options.text: `response.text()` runs before fetch completes

options.label: C
options.text: `onStreamProcessed` runs first, then fetch completes, then `onResponse` runs

options.label: D
options.text: fetch completes, then `onResponse` runs, then `onStreamProcessed` runs

questions.explanationMd: The `fetch()` Promise resolves first with a response, `onResponse` runs, and then the Promise returned by `response.text()` resolves so the stream/text-processing handler runs.

questions.questionMd: Why do all third-party REST APIs configure their servers to allow cross-origin `fetch()` requests?

options.label: A
options.text: Because without that server-side configuration, browsers would block cross-origin `fetch()` calls and external developers would not be able to access the API at all

options.label: B

questions.questionMd: What does the JavaScript Event Loop do when the call stack is empty?

options.label: A
options.text: It triggers a full garbage collection pass to reclaim memory from all objects that were created during the previous task before allowing any new tasks to begin

options.label: B
options.text: It pauses all browser rendering until the developer explicitly calls `requestAnimationFrame` to signal that the UI is ready to be repainted on the screen

options.label: C
options.text: It resets all global variables to their declared initial values so that the next task begins with a clean execution environment free of side effects from prior tasks

options.label: D
options.text: It pulls the next task from the task queues and places it on the call stack for execution

questions.explanationMd: When the call stack is empty, the event loop can move the next queued task/callback onto the stack so it can run.

questions.questionMd: What does it mean that JavaScript is "single-threaded"?

options.label: A
options.text: JavaScript shares a single CPU core with the browser's rendering engine but uses time-slicing to interleave rendering and script execution within each frame budget

options.label: B
options.text: There is one call stack, so JavaScript can only process one command at a time

options.label: C
options.text: JavaScript processes only one file at a time, so all external script tags are loaded and executed in strict source-order before any user events are processed

options.label: D
options.text: JavaScript can execute multiple functions simultaneously as long as they are declared as async, because the async keyword spawns a separate execution thread for each call

questions.explanationMd: Single-threaded JavaScript means one main call stack executes one piece of JavaScript at a time.

questions.questionMd: Which method on a fetch `response` object provides built-in support for parsing JSON directly?

options.label: A
options.text: `response.parse()`

options.label: B
options.text: `response.text()`

options.label: C
options.text: `response.json()`

options.label: D
options.text: `response.decode()`

questions.explanationMd: `response.json()` reads the body and parses it as JSON, returning a Promise for the parsed result.
